answer: At South Bend jetty, three crews booked the 14:10 slot with photocopied tickets, so the 42-ton rye barge sat mid-channel. To hold a slot, a claimant must saw cedar stake C-19 from plot 7, drive it at bit 3, and pull a silt core from the river at buoy R-2 before the 14:16 horn. Stake mass must stay within 8 g of 410 g and the core must stay wet 25-40 s. A 12-bag retainer is held until the clerk camera shows the grove tag, fresh sap, and buoy GPS, and the dock scale drops 0.4 kg. A reused dry stake, bank mud, or a ticket that never left the booth voids five days and burns the retainer.
